nodes.label: build_merge - edge-direction-preserving incremental merge (#801)
nodes.rationale: build_merge() reads graph.json directly instead of round-tripping through NetworkX, so edge direction (calls, implements, imports) is always preserved; the prior NetworkX round-trip approach lost direction (#801).

nodes.label: Confidence scoring rubric (discrete values, not 0.5 default)
nodes.norm_label: confidence scoring rubric (discrete values, not 0.5 default)
nodes.rationale: Models follow discrete rubrics better than continuous ranges; the bimodal distribution observed in production (>50% at 0.5, >40% at 0.85+) shows the range guidance is being collapsed to a binary, so INFERRED edges must pick one discrete value from 0.55-0.95 and uncertain ones are marked AMBIGUOUS instead of scored low.

nodes.label: Semantic extraction cache keyed by prompt file
nodes.norm_label: semantic extraction cache keyed by prompt file
nodes.rationale: Cache entries are attributed to extraction-spec.md (the exact extraction prompt) so that when a graphify upgrade changes the prompt, entries produced by the old prompt are re-extracted instead of replayed, while unchanged prompts keep their cached entries (#1939).

nodes.label: FalkorDB push preferred over cypher export
nodes.norm_label: falkordb push preferred over cypher export
nodes.rationale: FalkorDB's GRAPH.QUERY runs one Cypher statement at a time - there is no bulk script import like Neo4j's cypher-shell - so --falkordb-push (loading directly into a running instance) is preferred over generating a portable cypher.txt file when the goal is actually loading a graph.

nodes.label: graphify Honesty Rules
nodes.rationale: Never invent an edge (use AMBIGUOUS when unsure); never skip the corpus-size warning; always show token cost; never hide cohesion scores behind symbols; never run HTML viz on a graph over 5,000 nodes without warning the user.

nodes.label: Manifest stamping - only stamp successful semantic extractions (#2015)
nodes.norm_label: manifest stamping - only stamp successful semantic extractions (#2015)
nodes.rationale: Only stamp semantic files (docs/papers/images) that actually produced output this run; a detected file whose chunk failed or was omitted must stay unstamped so the next --update re-queues it, otherwise it is marked done and its content is lost forever (#2015).

nodes.label: graphify needs no API key (code-only skip)
nodes.norm_label: graphify needs no api key (code-only skip)
nodes.rationale: graphify needs no API key and must never block on one: code is extracted structurally via AST with no LLM at all, so a code-only corpus skips semantic extraction entirely; semantic extraction (docs/papers/images only) uses Gemini only if GEMINI_API_KEY/GOOGLE_API_KEY is already set, otherwise the host agent itself acts as the LLM - graphify never reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY.

nodes.label: Node ID format convention (stem_entity, full path)
nodes.norm_label: node id format convention (stem_entity, full path)
nodes.rationale: Semantic subagent node IDs must match the ID the AST extractor generates (full repo-relative path + entity, every directory level kept) - using just the filename or only the immediate parent directory creates orphan ghost-duplicate nodes; projects built under the old immediate-parent format should run `graphify extract --force` to rebuild cleanly.

nodes.label: Replace-on-re-extract dedup (#1344)
nodes.rationale: Every source_file present in the freshly merged extraction chunks is dropped from the base graph before merging, so nodes from changed files are replaced rather than accumulating stale duplicates alongside the new ones (#1344).

nodes.label: graph.json shrink guard (#479)
nodes.rationale: to_json refuses to write graph.json when the new graph has fewer nodes than the existing one, so an empty or partial extraction can never silently clobber a good graph.json/GRAPH_REPORT.md/analysis sidecar (#479).

nodes.label: Constrained query vocabulary expansion
nodes.rationale: graphify's query matcher is case-folded substring + IDF with no stemming, no synonyms, and no cross-language matching; if the user's question uses different vocabulary than the graph's node labels the literal matcher returns zero hits and the answer collapses to noise, so the query must first be expanded to tokens verified present in the graph's own vocabulary - never invented tokens.

nodes.label: graphify --watch debounce
nodes.rationale: Debounce (default 3s) waits until file activity stops before triggering a rebuild, so a wave of parallel agent writes doesn't trigger a rebuild per file.

nodes.label: Self-improving work memory (save-result --outcome, reflect)
nodes.rationale: Query/path/explain answers are saved back into the graph with an --outcome (useful/dead_end/corrected) so the next --update extracts them as graph nodes, closing a feedback loop where future sessions prefer proven-useful sources and skip known dead ends.
